From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs - initial redlines

Ben / Ellen — reviewed NovumCare's tracked changes. High-level comments and proposed markup: 

1) Controller/Processor: Accept processor posture. Proposed clause: "Company acts as controller of Customer Data; Redwood acts as processor for Customer Data processed for inference and hosting; Redwood will only use Customer Data for Model Improvement or Training with explicit Customer written consent and a separate MSA addendum." Add explicit definition for "Model Improvement" and "Training" to avoid ambiguity.

2) Training carveout: Suggest adding a two-tier opt-in: (a) anonymized aggregate telemetry for platform performance (non-personal) — allowed by default; (b) any use for model improvement that might include derived data — requires opt-in via Order Form checkbox and separate DPA exhibit.

3) SCCs mapping: NovumCare's SCCs spreadsheet needs a column mapping to Redwood's subprocessors and hosting regions. Priyom, please produce a brief mapping of our regions and subprocessors by Wed EOD so we can populate.

4) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): Recommend a narrow TIA template that enumerates permitted destination countries and the party responsible for additional cross-border assessments. We should also limit liability carveouts for data residency exceptions.

5) Evidence: we can provide SOC2 Type II summary and a signed attestation for TLS + KMS key rotation cadence. For on-prem/private deployments we can provide architecture notes in a separate technical annex.

I'll prepare a clean redline (MS Word) with the suggested language and send by Tue AM so Ben can share with NovumCare pre-call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Laura / Ben / Ellen — quick privacy notes to feed into the clean redline: 

- Data categories: Ensure the DPA explicitly lists categories of Customer Data vs. Customer Content vs. Platform Telemetry. This reduces downstream disagreement about "training" scope.
- De-identification: If NovumCare wants an opt-in for model training, require a visible de-identification standard (hashing + tokenization) and a retention window (e.g., delete training artifacts after 18 months unless otherwise agreed).
- Subprocessor notifications: propose a 30-day notice for new subprocessors except for emergency security fixes; include a review window for high-risk subprocessors.
- Transfer assessment: for EU-origin data, the TIA should require a documented risk assessment and a fallback routing policy to EU region if additional risk is identified.

I'll attach a basic mapping file with regions/subprocessors at 10:30 PT for Laura to merge.

Priyom Das
Privacy & Compliance Manager
priyom_das@redwood.ai
